title: Parameter rules and the noise-free veto

items.title: Noise-level-free parameter-choice rule
items.statement:
Fix a compact Hilbert inverse model $K:X\to Y$ and a family of reconstruction
maps $(R_\alpha)_{\alpha>0}$, with each $R_\alpha:Y\to X$, both held fixed. A
deterministic parameter-choice rule is a function
$\alpha:Y\to(0,\infty)$. It is **noise-level-free** (also called **heuristic**)
when the value $\alpha(z)$ for an observed datum $z\in Y$ uses only $K$, the
fixed family, and $z$; it does not take the exact datum or a noise bound
$\delta$ as input. Here $\delta\ge0$ is a valid noise bound for $z$ and an
exact datum $y$ when $\|z-y\|_Y\le\delta$. The resulting reconstruction is
$R_{\alpha(z)}z$.

references.locator: Chapter 4, Definition 4.4, PDF p. 34; categories of parameter-choice rules.

items.title: Bakushinskii veto for discontinuous pseudoinverses
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $K:X\to Y$ be a compact linear operator between
real or complex Hilbert spaces over one scalar field, with Hilbert-space
Moore–Penrose inverse $K^\dagger:D(K^\dagger)\to X$. Suppose $K^\dagger$ is
discontinuous on $D(K^\dagger)$ with its norm inherited from $Y$. Let
$(R_\alpha)_{\alpha>0}$ be maps $Y\to X$ such that
$R_\alpha y\to K^\dagger y$ for every $y\in D(K^\dagger)$ as
$\alpha\downarrow0$, and let $\alpha:Y\to(0,\infty)$ be a deterministic
noise-level-free rule. For each exact datum $y\in D(K^\dagger)$ and
$\delta>0$, set $E_y(\delta):=\sup\{\|R_{\alpha(z)}z-K^\dagger y\|_X:z\in Y,\ \|z-y\|_Y\le\delta\}$.
If $E_y(\delta)\to0$ as $\delta\downarrow0$ for every $y\in D(K^\dagger)$,
then $K^\dagger$ is continuous on $D(K^\dagger).$ Thus, when $K^\dagger$ is
discontinuous, no such noise-level-free rule yields worst-case convergence
over each exact datum's full admissible error balls. The limit is required
separately for each exact datum, not uniformly over $y$. This veto does not
exclude convergence on restricted solution or error classes, stochastic noise
models, or finite-dimensional problems.

title: Parameter rules and the noise-free veto — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A finite-grid L-curve selects an interior parameter
items.statement:
Take $A=I_2\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}$, $b=e_1$, and the strictly increasing grid
$1/9<1<9$. Apply the discrete maximum-curvature L-curve selector to this input.
The Tikhonov solution at $\lambda$ is $x_\lambda=(1+\lambda)^{-1}e_1$, so all
three residual and solution norms are positive and the selector returns the
middle grid value $\lambda=1$. This finite-grid data-driven choice is made
without a noise-level input, and it carries no universal optimality claim. The
matrix is finite-dimensional, so the discontinuity hypothesis of the
Bakushinskii veto is absent.

references.title: Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 5: Regularization Parameter Choice
references.locator: Slides 10–14, PDF pp. 9–13: log-log L-curve, curvature, and maximum-curvature corner.

items.title: Noise underestimation defeats a truncated singular-value rule
items.statement:
**False claim.** Let $X=Y=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ with standard basis
$(e_j)_{j\ge1}$, let $Kx=(x_j/j)_{j\ge1}$, and for $\alpha>0$ define
$R_\alpha z=\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor1/\alpha\rfloor}kz_ke_k$, with the empty sum
used when the upper limit is $0$. Define the data-only noise proxy by
$\widehat\delta(0)=1$ and $\widehat\delta(z)=\min\{1,\|z\|_2^2\}$ for $z\ne0$,
and set $\alpha(z)=\widehat\delta(z)$. The false claim is that this compact
operator, pointwise regularizing family, and deterministic noise-level-free
rule satisfy, for every exact datum $y\in D(K^\dagger)$,
$\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\sup\{\|R_{\alpha(z)}z-K^\dagger y\|_2:z\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R),\ \|z-y\|_2\le\delta\}=0$.

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Theorem 4.8
references.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.8 and proof, PDF p. 37: the general data-only choice obstruction.

references.title: Ferdia Sherry, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes 2024, Theorem 3.12
references.locator: Section 3.2.3, Theorem 3.12 and proof, PDF pp. 33–34: the general data-only choice obstruction.

items.title: Conditional stability on a power-source class
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $K:X\to Y$ be a compact operator of infinite rank
between real or complex Hilbert spaces over one scalar field. Let
$(s_j,v_j,u_j)_{j\ge1}$ be a positive singular system with $s_j>0$,
$s_j\to0$, $\|v_j\|_X=\|u_j\|_Y=1$, and $Kv_j=s_ju_j$. For $\rho>0$ let
$M_\rho=X_{1,\rho}(K)=\{|K|w:w\in X,\ \|w\|_X\le\rho\}$ and define
$\varepsilon_K(M_\rho,\delta)=\sup\{\|x\|_X:x\in M_\rho,\
\|Kx\|_Y\le\delta\}$. Then
$\varepsilon_K(M_\rho,\delta)\le\sqrt{\rho\delta}$ for every $\delta\ge0$,
with equality at $\delta_j=\rho s_j^2$ for each $j$, witnessed by
$x_j=\rho s_jv_j$. Although $K^\dagger$ is discontinuous on its full domain,
this modulus tends to zero on the restricted source class $M_\rho$; this
conditional stability makes no claim of universal noise-level-free
convergence.

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Theorems 4.11–4.12
references.locator: Section 4.2, Theorems 4.11–4.12, PDF p. 40: power-source conditional modulus and singular-direction attainment.
